title: The identity component of a finite-type group scheme over an arbitrary field is an open and closed subgroup
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field] and let $G$ be a group scheme over $k$ [def-sc-group-scheme] of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Let $e\in |G|$ be the image of the unique point of $\operatorname{Spec}k$ under the identity section. The connected component $G^0$ containing $e$, that is, the maximal connected subset containing $e$ [def-weil-connected-scheme], is open and closed in $G$. With its open-subscheme structure [def-weil-open-immersion], $G^0$ is a connected group scheme, and the inclusion $j:G^0\to G$ is a homomorphism and a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion], hence a closed subgroup scheme [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup]. No perfectness or algebraic closedness of $k$ and no reducedness or smoothness of $G$ is assumed.

source.place: Tag 0B7R (proposition-connected-component), canonical closed identity subgroup. In the finite-type case it is also open: Milne, literature/milne-algebraic-groups_iAG2017.pdf, Proposition 1.34, printed pp.16-17, with the finite component discussion in 1.30-1.33. Project implementations: WeilConjectures/AlgebraicGeometry/GroupScheme/Basic.lean:250-260, 434-500, 548-576.

proof.text: Write $C$ for the connected component containing $e$. Apply [lem-trf-finite-type-component-open-qc] to the finite-type $k$-scheme $G$ and its point $e$. Thus $C$ is open and its open subscheme $H=(C,\mathcal O_G|_C)$ is nonempty and connected. Denote its open immersion by $j:H\to G$.

source.place: Tag 057K (lemma-local-local-structure-finite-type), the connected-component paragraph; its general Noetherian component argument is recorded by the cited node.

proof.text: The component $C$ is also closed. Indeed any separation of its closure into two relatively clopen pieces restricts to a separation of $C$ [def-weil-connected-scheme]. Connectedness puts all of $C$ in one piece, whose relative closedness then puts its closure there; thus the closure is connected and maximality of $C$ gives $\overline C=C$. We will also use the elementary observation that a continuous image of a connected space is connected: a separation of the image pulls back to a separation of the source, and both pieces are nonempty if the image pieces are. Finally any connected subset $D$ containing $e$ lies in $C$: the union $D\cup C$ is connected, since in a clopen separation both connected subsets must lie on the side containing $e$; maximality then gives $D\cup C=C$.

source.place: Tags 004S (definition-connected-components), 004T (lemma-connected-components); lemma-image-connected-space. These elementary arguments are written out here.

proof.text: Since the image of the identity section $e_G:\operatorname{Spec}k\to G$ is contained in $C$, [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-factors-through-open-subscheme] gives a unique $k$-morphism $e_H:\operatorname{Spec}k\to H$ with $j e_H=e_G$. (It is over $k$ because composition with the structure map of $H$ is that of $G$.) The scheme $\operatorname{Spec}k$ is geometrically connected: after every extension $K/k$ its base change is $\operatorname{Spec}K$, a nonempty one-point space. Apply [lem-trf-geometrically-connected-image-criterion] to $e_H$ and the connected $H$ of step 1. Consequently $H$ is geometrically connected over $k$.

source.place: Tag 0B7R (proposition-connected-component), the identity-section and geometric-connectedness argument, using Varieties Tag 056R (lemma-geometrically-connected-criterion).

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-geometrically-connected-product-components] with $X=Y=H$. As $H$ is geometrically connected and connected, $H\times_k H$ has precisely one connected component and is nonempty (it has the point $(e_H,e_H)$), so it is connected. Restrict multiplication to $f=m_G\circ(j\times j):H\times_k H\to G$. By step 2 its image is connected; the identity axiom gives $f(e_H,e_H)=e$, so its image lies in $C$. By [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-factors-through-open-subscheme] there is a unique $k$-morphism $m_H:H\times_k H\to H$ with $j m_H=m_G(j\times j)$.

source.place: Tag 0B7R (proposition-connected-component), multiplication paragraph, using Varieties Tag 0385 (lemma-bijection-connected-components); factorization through the open subscheme uses Schemes Tag 01HI (lemma-restrict-map-to-opens).

proof.text: The inverse $i_G$ fixes $e$ by the inverse and unit axioms [def-sc-group-scheme]. The image of $i_Gj:H\to G$ is connected by step 2 and contains $e$, so it is contained in $C$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-factors-through-open-subscheme] to obtain a unique $k$-morphism $i_H:H\to H$ with $j i_H=i_Gj$.

The factorization uniqueness in [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-factors-through-open-subscheme] implies that $j$ is a monomorphism: two maps to $H$ with equal composites to $G$ are the two factorizations of that composite. Check every group-object diagram after composing with $j$. Associativity becomes $m_G(m_G(j\times j)\times j)=m_G(j\times m_G(j\times j))$ on $H\times_kH\times_kH$; the two unit laws become $m_G(e_G,j)=j=m_G(j,e_G)$; and the inverse laws become $m_G(i_Gj,j)\Delta=e_G p=m_G(j,i_Gj)\Delta$, where $p:H\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ and $\Delta$ is the diagonal. These are exactly the diagrams of the given group scheme [def-sc-group-scheme]. Cancel $j$ to obtain the diagrams for $(H,m_H,e_H,i_H)$. Thus $H$ is a group scheme, and $j$ is a homomorphism by the defining equality for $m_H$.

source.place: Tag 0B7R (proposition-connected-component), subgroup assertion; Tag 0G8L (lemma-closed-subgroup-scheme), restriction of the group diagrams.

proof.text: The open immersion $j$ is an immersion: factor it as the identity closed immersion of $H$ followed by $j$ [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Its image is $C$, closed by step 2, so [lem-weil-pbc-immersion-closed-image-closed-immersion] makes $j$ a closed immersion. For every $k$-algebra $R$, $j(R)$ is injective by the uniqueness from step 6, and preserves multiplication, identity and inversion by the defining factorizations. Its image is therefore a subgroup of $G(R)$, proving the closed-subgroup assertion in [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup]. Since $H$ has underlying set $C$ with its subspace topology, it is exactly the required connected group scheme $G^0$.

source.place: Tag 0B7R (proposition-connected-component), closed-subgroup conclusion; Schemes Tag 01IQ (lemma-immersion-when-closed, literature/stacks-project/schemes.tex).
